articles.headline: Aaron Glenn defends clock management after Jets' collapse
articles.description: The Jets blew their biggest fourth-quarter lead in six years in a 20-17 overtime loss to the Packers, with coach Aaron Glenn facing scrutiny for his clock management.
articles.body:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- The New York Jets were 11 minutes away from their first 2-0 start since 2015, enjoying a 10-point lead on Sunday, but a series of breakdowns and questionable coaching decisions turned the "White Out" at MetLife Stadium into a fade-to-black outcome.

The Jets blew their biggest fourth-quarter lead in six years and fell to the Green Bay Packers in overtime 20-17, with coach Aaron Glenn being scrutinized for his clock management.

"To to be honest, I'm highly upset," Glenn said. "(It's a) tough way to lose a game. There are a number of things that go through my head that, man, we have to fix. And it's always tough when you feel like you were right there in the thick of it and then you didn't overcome, and you let the other team overcome and win.

"That's tough, but I will say this: This loss is not going to define who we are and what we're about. I will say that. And it's not OK. And our guys are going to take it like that. It's not OK."

The game was almost impossible to lose.

The Jets let the Packers become the first team on record (since 1941) to win a game with less than 200 total yards (199), more than 100 penalty yards (133) and a negative turnover margin (-1), according to ESPN Research. Previously, teams were 0-44 in that situation.

Late in the game, Glenn made two strategic decisions that backfired.

At the end of regulation, Glenn failed to call a timeout that would've given his offense one last shot to march for a potential game-winning field goal. In the end, the Jets wasted the final minute without getting the ball back.

Packers wide receiver Christian Watson was tackled at the Jets' 45-yard line with 1:02 remaining, leaving Green Bay with a fourth-and-5. Glenn, who had two timeouts left, didn't stop the clock.

The Packers wound up taking an intentional delay-of-game penalty. After a 10-second run off and a timeout by each team, the fourth quarter ended with Jordan Love being sacked on a Hail Mary play that started with two second left.

Even Packers coach Matt LaFleur was perplexed by Glenn's decision.

"Oh yeah, I was (surprised)," LaFleur said. "I was really confused by that, and that's why we called a timeout and tried a Hail Mary."

Glenn defended his strategy, saying, "I think they could have punted the ball and put us in a backed-up situation right there. So that was the reason why" they let the time run down.

The Jets won the overtime coin toss and decided to take the ball. Most coaches prefer to get the ball last because it provides an informational advantage under the updated overtime rules, allowing them to know exactly what their team needs to win or extend the game.

Glenn said he wanted the ball because "you can really control the clock. You can control exactly how they're going to play offense once you go and score." He wanted to score and put pressure on Green Bay to score, except "it didn't happen the way I planned."

No, it didn't.

The Jets went three-and-out, with two sacks and a false-star

articles.headline: NFL Week 2: Takeaways, questions, fantasy spin for Sunday games
articles.description: Our NFL Nation reporters react to all the action, answering the biggest questions coming out of each Sunday game. Here's what we learned from Week 2.
articles.body:
In the early window of NFL Week 2 on Sunday, last week's offensive explosion seemed like a thing of the distant past.

Five teams failed to reach double-digits points, including both the Bears and Vikings at a rainy Soldier Field. The Panthers forced five turnovers against the Falcons, while the Patriots cemented their win over the Steelers with a fumble return for a touchdown. The highest-scoring matchup of the early window (44 points) came between the Titans and Eagles, which ended on a game-winning touchdown grab by Philly's Darius Cooper.

In the late window Sunday, wide receiver Jaylen Waddle made up for his disappointing Broncos debut with 138 receiving yards against the Jaguars. Meanwhile, the 49ers dominated the Dolphins in their first game back from Melbourne, Australia. And the Seahawks won their second straight game with backup quarterback Drew Lock.

Our NFL Nation reporters reacted to all the action, answering lingering questions coming out of each game and detailing everything else you need to know for teams that played Sunday. Fantasy football analysts Matt Bowen and Tristan Cockcroft also have fantasy takeaways from each matchup. Let's get to it.

Jump to:

JAX-DEN | CLE-TB | PHI-TEN

GB-NYJ | CIN-HOU | MIN-CHI

NO-BAL | CAR-ATL | PIT-NE

Catch up on Thursday's game:

DET-BUF

Seattle 31, Arizona 7

Catch up on the action: Box score | Recap

Seahawks

Will Drew Lock have the Seahawks unbeaten by the time Sam Darnold returns? For the second straight week, the Seahawks showed they have the dominant defense, offensive weaponry and good enough backup quarterback to survive a stretch without their starter. Lock was 19-of-26 for 235 yards, three TDs and no turnovers. The Seahawks hope Darnold can practice this week, which suggests he might not have to miss more than another game or two. Seattle plays at Washington -- which lost Jayden Daniels to an elbow injury Sunday -- before hosting the 0-2 Chargers in Week 4.

Key stat to know: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year, finished with nine catches for 155 yards and has 11 games with at least 100 receiving yards since the start of last season. Per ESPN Research, that's the most in the NFL. Smith-Njigba also became the third Seahawk with 150-plus receiving yards and three receiving TDs in a game, joining Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent (twice). -- Brady Henderson

Next game: at Commanders (Sunday, 1 p.m. ET)

Cardinals

What went wrong for the defense in the second half? Arizona's defense went from stopping the run on a regular basis in the first half to hardly containing it in the second. Arizona gave up 43 rushing yards in the first two quarters, stopping the Seahawks twice within 4 yards of the end zone in the second quarter -- including on fourth-and-1 from the 1. But whatever worked in the first half didn't in the second, as Arizona allowed 109 yards in the final two quarters.

Sept. 18: Josh Allen puts league on notice with 40-point night

by Adam Rank

We had one of the highest-scoring Week 1s in NFL history last week. There was no way we could possibly top that, yeah? Well, I've got news for you, the Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions accepted the challenge and put up massive numbers on Thursday night.

Josh Allen led the way with more than 40 points to get your week started. We went into the draft season saying Allen was in his own tier and he's proving it early on. Allen had over 300 total yards and five total touchdowns. Allen is the third player in NFL history with nine total touchdowns and no turnovers in his team's first two games of the season. The other two were Patrick Mahomes in 2018 and Peyton Manning in 2013. Both went on to win MVP. Manning's Broncos also set the NFL record for most points in the season.

The Bills are the first team to record 35 points and more than 400 yards of offense in both of their first two games of the season since the Packers in 2020. The Bills have also scored five touchdowns in five red zone drives.

My guy Tristan H. Cockcroft pointed out during our in-game group chat that Allen broke the record for most fantasy points scored in the first two weeks of the season. Breaking the record of ... Ryan Fitzpatrick, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers version (as noted by Field Yates, who knew the answer to Tristan's trivia question).

Our group chat also had an interesting conversation about James Cook III. Is he a trade-high candidate because it's Josh Allen's offense, including goal-line carries -- or do you try to get more shares of Cook, if possible? Put me in the convo for more shares. I want as much of this Bills offense as possible. Especially if D.J. Moore is going to miss time. (Note: Moore is considered day-to-day)

Keon Coleman and Khalil Shakir both had six targets. Joshua Palmer had a 43-yard TD reception on his lone target.

articles.headline: Drew Lock connects for 3 TDs with Jaxon Smith-Njigba, Seahawks roll past Cardinals 31-7
articles.description: — Drew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a stellar first start subbing for the injured Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks continued their dominance over the Arizona Cardinals with a 31-7 win on Sunday.
articles.body:
GLENDALE, Ariz. -- — Drew Lock threw for 235 yards and three touchdowns to Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a stellar first start subbing for the injured Sam Darnold and the Seattle Seahawks continued their dominance over the Arizona Cardinals with a 31-7 win on Sunday.


              The defending Super Bowl champions have now won 10 straight over their NFC West rival dating to 2022 and closed this one by scoring the final 24 points. Smith-Njigba finished with nine catches for 155 yards and the career-high three TDs in one of the best performances of his four-year career.


              Arizona has lost eight straight games at home in a streak that's lasted 360 days. The Cardinals finished with just 150 total yards.


              Lock got off to a good start, taking advantage of a busted coverage by the Cardinals' secondary and hitting a wide open Smith-Njigba in stride for an 82-yard touchdown on the team's second offensive play of the game for a 7-0 lead. Early in the third quarter, he found the reigning AP Offensive Player of the Year on a crossing route for a 7-yard score and a 14-7 advantage.


              That Seattle touchdown was set up by some good fortune on the opening kickoff of the second half. Rashid Shaheed fumbled on the return, but teammate Chazz Surratt picked up the ball and ran 35 yards all the way to the Arizona 37.


              Seattle safety Julian Love intercepted Jacoby Brissett on the ensuing drive, making a spectacular sliding catch as he got his hand under the ball just before it hit the ground. It gave the Seahawks (2-0) great field position again at the Arizona 44, which they parlayed into Jason Myers' 33-yard field goal and a 17-7 lead.


              Smith-Njigba's third touchdown came early in the fourth quarter when Lock threw a perfectly placed ball for a 12-yard strike and a 24-7 lead.


              The Cardinals (1-1) opened the season with an impressive 26-14 road win over the Chargers in first-year coach Mike LaFleur's debut, but couldn't recreate that success against the talented Seahawks defense. Brissett threw a 2-yard touchdown to All-Pro tight end Trey McBride to tie the game at 7-all on the first play of the second quarter.


              Seattle had a chance to retake the lead late in the second quarter but couldn't ram the ball into the end zone from the 1-yard line on fourth down. The game stayed tied going into halftime, but it was all Seahawks after the break.


              Brissett threw for 95 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Rookie Jeremiyah Love led the team with 29 yards rushing and McBride caught eight passes for 41 yards.


              Lock made his first start since the final week of the 2024 season, taking over for Darnold, who suffered a glute injury in the opener against New England. The 29-year-old played most of that game and performed well, completing 16 of 22 passes for 187 yards and a touchdown.

articles.headline: Christian Pulisic starts, gets first Milan goal of 2026 in win
articles.description: AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.
articles.headlineJa: クリスチャン・プリシッチが先発、勝利を収めた試合で2026年初のミランでのゴールを記録
articles.descriptionJa: ACミランは日曜日、サン・シーロでレッチェに3-0で勝利し、セリエAでの無敗記録を伸ばしました。
articles.body:
AC Milan continued their unbeaten run in Serie A with a 3-0 win over Lecce at San Siro on Sunday.

Christian Pulisic fired Ruben Amorim's side ahead early on before second-half goals from Adrien Rabiot and Diego Moreira wrapped up the win.

Milan now go into the international break fifth in the standings thanks to their third win of the campaign alongside two draws.

Lecce looked to strike in the opening stages as Joel Monteiro and Ivan Ilic both went close, but Milan took the lead in the 14th minute through Pulisic.

A brilliant piece of skill saw the United States striker coolly bring down Strahinja Pavlovic's cross-field pass with a single touch before moving the ball onto his left foot and firing into the bottom corner.

The goal was Pulisic's first for Milan of the calendar year after his red-hot start to the 2025 campaign came to a screeching halt in 2026. The U.S. star was not selected by Mauricio Pochettino for the squad that will play four friendlies in the upcoming international window.

Pulisic had made two other appearances with Milan this season in all competitions, coming off the bench in both at halftime. His last goal for Milan had been in December 2025 in a league win over Verona and he scored once for the U.S. in a friendly against Senegal before the start of the 2026 World Cup.

"It hasn't been an easy year," Pulisic said after the game. "I'm happy about the goal today, but right now all that matters is to keep winning."

Milan had won only one home game since March and was booed off the field in a 2-0 home loss to Benfica in the Europa League on Wednesday.

Mike Maignan was called into action to make the save from Kialonda Gaspar, and before the break Milan went close in quick succession as Koni De Winter nodded wide before Pavlovic's effort was stopped by Wladimiro Falcone.

Pervis Estupiñán had a shot blocked after the restart, but Milan doubled their advantage 61 minutes in through Rabiot, who completed a team goal following a quick exchange with Gonçalo Ramos before slotting the ball past Falcone.

Estupinan fired wide as the hosts looked to build on their lead, and just moments later Moreira scored their third goal of the evening.

The substitute won the ball just inside Lecce's half and raced down the left flank before cutting into the box, where he evaded the visiting defense and hit a low finish underneath Falcone in the 73rd minute.

Information from PA and The Associated Press was used in this recap.
